parallel.requirements: Recognized the same CLI, byte-for-byte output, std-only Rust, Cargo project, root test7.rs, and black-box C++ binary requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and local integration, then delegated an expansive verifier workflow with differential shards, audit lenses, and adversarial verification children.
parallel.implementation: Created a Rust earcut-style module tree, entry file, CLI parsing, spiral generation, and fixes for bare rustc and pipe behavior, then rebuilt and retested the artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Placed the project in /output with Cargo and rustc build outputs; after workflow launch it edited and rebuilt the live entry source/executable while children were using it.
parallel.verification: Ran local rustc/cargo builds, byte comparisons over n ranges and edge cases, then launched a large workflow verifier whose children produced differential and audit results but no aggregate synthesis before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 39/39, but the agent process timed out with no final response and the workflow did not return a final synthesized verdict to the parent.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust porting, CLI, output fidelity, std-only dependency, Cargo structure, and root test7.rs requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in a single parent trajectory with no delegation, owning implementation, build, verification, and final response end to end.
serial.implementation: Built the Rust project and earcut-style modules, fixed import/build issues, implemented atoi and output formatting, and produced a passing executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the module tree and root entry point in /output, verified no external dependencies, and delivered a final response describing the build and checks.
serial.verification: Ran rustc and cargo builds, compared outputs over broad n ranges and argument edge cases, checked dependencies and formatting, then closed normally.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished work is visible; process completed normally and official evaluation passed 39/39.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run worked from the prompt requirements for std-only Rust, Cargo structure, root test7.rs, CLI parity, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received and followed the same prompt requirements for the Rust port and output fidelity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference explains the official result; both official evaluations passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and then delegated broad verifier work through a workflow after local progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no workflow or delegation and kept implementation, verification, and closure in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added many verifier owners after implementation; serial had a single owner and avoided coordination overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow prompts supplied extensive context and read-only verification tasks, but the candidate artifact later changed while children were active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained task context locally and did not need child briefs, handoffs, or cross-agent interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child-context and live-artifact boundaries; serial avoided those boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the module tree and entry file, compiled, found two local defects, edited them, and reran regression.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the same style of module tree locally and verified the finished binaries in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached passing implementations; the concrete implementation difference is not outcome-relevant.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow generated child starts and results but the parent never reached a final aggregate synthesis or final answer before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed the local work and wrote a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle stalled at workflow aggregation and closure; serial closed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After workflow launch, the parent edited test7.rs and rebuilt outputs while children were verifying the artifact, producing a moving verification target.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made source and build changes within one actor and then checked the final files and dependency state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a live shared-artifact rewrite boundary; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had strong local checks plus workflow differential/audit activity and passed official evaluation 39/39.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local differential/build checks and passed official evaluation 39/39.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both were accepted officially; parallel verification was broader but unfinished as an aggregate workflow, while serial verification was bounded and closed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 37 subagents and overran the agent process budget, ending with return code 143 and zero remaining retry budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 651.145 seconds, return code 0, with 1747 seconds of retry budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget and closure are the key process difference: parallel passed but timed out empty, while serial passed and closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: both parallel and serial passed 39 of 39 official testcases. The concrete difference is process behavior: parallel spent the remaining window in a broad verifier workflow and rewrote live artifacts during verification, then timed out without final closure; serial completed locally and returned normally.
parallel_contributors: Broad verifier workflow and live artifact rewrite created adverse process overhead but did not change official pass/fail outcome.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation, verification, and final response completed normally.
No delegation or workflow child activity was present in the control trajectory.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary implementation defect explains an outcome split because there is no outcome split.
evaluator_effects: Official completed evaluator records are aligned: both modes passed all 39 evaluated testcases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels describe adverse parallel process consequences only

candidates.reason: Rejected because the parallel parent directly owned and wrote the Rust implementation before delegating verification.
Rejected because the implementation was a parent-owned module tree, not separately owned component outputs needing cross-agent integration.
Rejected because the parent created the Cargo project, root test7.rs entry point, and executable artifacts before official evaluation.
Rejected because the parent owned implementation, build, local testing, and workflow launch; the problem was later fan-out budget use, not an ownerless pipeline.
Rejected because implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent implemented and tested before the workflow.
Rejected because there was no completed investigation-only phase that delayed productive implementation; productive code work happened first.
Rejected because the directly evidenced allocation event is broad verifier fan-out exhausting budget, not auxiliary work starving implementation capacity.

The parent launched a verifier workflow with broad parallel differential jobs, audit jobs, and nested per-finding verifier fan-out after the artifact was already locally built and tested. That collective breadth consumed the finite run budget before normal closure, leaving the process timed out even though official evaluation passed.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier fleet displaced normal closure: the parallel process ended with return code 143 and zero remaining budget, and no final response was written, while the official artifact still passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing aggregate verifier return is downstream of the same over-broad workflow fan-out; no independent verifier-result lifecycle has separate anchors and consequence.

Rejected because children were verification/audit actors, not separate implementers producing interoperating components with absent contracts.
Rejected because no known parent finding disappeared through a summary or transfer and caused repeated work; the main issue is budget and live artifact state.
Rejected because the parent never received a large final handoff that it failed to reduce; the workflow failed to reach aggregate synthesis before timeout.
Rejected because although children saw changing artifacts, the concrete boundary is live deliverable rewrite, not a receiver acting on a stale transferred report.
Rejected because incompatible reports did not reach the parent and remain unadjudicated in a completion decision.
Rejected because the parent did not make an unsupported final completion decision; local checks existed and official evaluation passed.
Rejected because the repeated workflow starts were verifier tasks and adversarial checks, not replacement retries missing inherited checkpoints.

candidates.reason: Rejected because there is no separate parent stop/cancel action on an active required child before its needed result; timeout is part of the fan-out chain.
Rejected because the usable artifact had already been built and placed; the missing final response is a closure symptom of timeout rather than late artifact promotion.
Rejected because no delegated implementation change was merged only after integrated verification; implementation edits and rechecks stayed in the parent path.
Rejected because no child-owned implementation result needed to be retrieved or integrated into the final artifact.
Rejected because the absent aggregate return is downstream of the retained fan-out budget exhaustion episode, not an independent trapped verifier finding.
Rejected because any incomplete verifier children were not required implementation owners, and no separate takeover boundary is evidenced outside the fan-out timeout.
Rejected because completed child results were not ignored while the parent proceeded inconsistently; the run timed out before aggregate synthesis.
Rejected because the parent periodically inspected workflow progress; the adverse boundary is the broad workflow budget burn, not absence of monitoring.
Rejected because there were not concurrent component implementations in different files claiming overlapping behavior; verifier children were primarily auditing.
Rejected because no two live actors are shown editing the same file with one reconciling the other edit.
Rejected because the non-entry source edit was parent-owned and part of the same live rewrite episode; the entry source/executable makes Deliverable Overwrite the more specific label.

After the workflow children had been launched to use the /output artifact, the parent edited the required entry source and rebuilt the executable/build outputs. A verifier child then checked artifact freshness and re-read the entry source after an apparent concurrent change, showing a moving target rather than a frozen candidate.
candidates.realized_consequence: Verification provenance became unstable: live workflow children used, checked, and rebuilt against a changing entry source and executable instead of a fixed artifact snapshot.
candidates.near_match_reason: The narrower deliverable label applies because the overwritten objects included the direct entry source and executable/build artifacts, not merely unspecified shared workspace files.
